acme_ops: Hey team — after we flipped the customer-managed gateway into prod, our app started hitting a ton of 429s and some 502/503 spikes. We see this pattern: steady traffic, then a burst for ~20s, then widespread 429 with `retry-after` headers. No recent code changes on our side. Can you help triage?

Maya (Support): Thanks, sending to SRE. Do you have an example request id and the raw response body/header you saw?

acme_ops: Example: `x-request-id: acme-req-78f2`, response body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":7}`. Headers included `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 1712345678`. We also see ingress logs with `upstream response: 503` around same time.

Raj (SRE): Ok. Quick questions: are you using our hosted token routing or did you point the gateway to your own Redwood Private control plane? Also which ingress controller (nginx/traefik/envoy) are you using in the VPC?

acme_ops: We're on Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) and using nginx-ingress (k8s). Gateway runs as a DaemonSet fronting requests to the cluster.

Lina (Platform Eng): Two likely buckets: 1) Our rate limiter at the gateway is counting client bursts across multiple nodes and your k8s ingress is opening a lot of simultaneous connections, exhausting connection slots / upstream queue. 2) Kubernetes node-level limits (conntrack, ephemeral ports, ingress controller worker settings) causing 502s when upstream can't accept more.

Maya (Support): Can you reproduce with a short load test? If yes, please capture: ingress pod logs, gateway logs, and output of `kubectl describe ingress` around the time of error.

acme_ops: We ran a 30s burst (locust) — attached excerpt below:
```
[ingress] 2026-01-21T21:01:12Z INFO "GET /v1/generate" 200 123ms
[ingress] 2026-01-21T21:01:32Z WARN "GET /v1/generate" 429 5ms x-rate-limit-remaining:0
[gateway] 2026-01-21T21:01:33Z ERROR Ratelimiter deny token=acme-prod burst=45 rate=10
[gateway] 2026-01-21T21:01:33Z INFO forwarded to upstream: 502
```

Raj (SRE): That `burst=45` stands out. Gateway token-bucket got exhausted. Two immediate mitigations: lower client concurrency (client side): implement exponential backoff + jitter and limit concurrent open requests; and on the gateway/ingress: tune token bucket settings or increase per-customer quota temporarily.

Lina (Platform Eng): For nginx-ingress, there are helpful annotations: `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections`, `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps`, and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rpm`. If you're using the nginx rate-limiting module, it enforces per-worker limits which can interact oddly with our gateway. Also check `worker-processes` and `worker-connections` in the nginx config.

acme_ops: We tried adding `limit-rps: "120"` and `limit-connections: "200"`. After that the 503s dropped but 429s persisted.

Raj (SRE): Right — 429s are coming from the Redwood gateway rate limiter, not nginx. We can do two things: 1) Increase the customer's burst allowance in the gateway config (short term) or 2) Change gateway policy to allow short bursts by increasing bucket capacity or token refill rate. We need to know the traffic shape: average rps and typical burst size.

acme_ops: Typical steady rps is ~25, burst from web clients hits ~600 rps for 15s. So large short bursts.

Maya (Support): We're going to open an ACE (escalation) to adjust gateway policy while you deploy client-side throttling. If you can deploy a client-side token bucket limiting to ~200 concurrent requests with retries that will smooth things while we adjust service side.

Lina (Platform Eng): On the infra side, add these checks: kernel conntrack table (`sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max`), increase `fs.file-max` and `net.core.somaxconn`, and tune `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` if ephemeral ports exhausted. Example commands:
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=65535
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
```

Raj (SRE): Also ensure kube-proxy mode and NAT aren't causing stalls. If you see `TIME_WAIT` piling up, increase `tcp_tw_reuse` / `tcp_tw_recycle` (careful), and bump conntrack-town.

acme_ops: Good to know. Any guidance on how our customer-managed gateway counts quota vs the cluster? Are requests counted at the gateway ingress only?

Maya (Support): In Private mode, quota & rate-limits are enforced at the gateway (edge). The gateway considers the token per API key and applies a token bucket across the key aggregated across all gateways talking to the control plane. If you run additional gateway replicas, they still coordinate for quota windows. If you ramp bursts across many clients simultaneously, the aggregated rate can hit the quota quickly.

Raj (SRE): We can temporarily bump the per-api-key `burst` to accommodate your 15s spikes while you implement client rate limiting. I'll add a bounded increase and set a revert window (24h) to avoid long-term cost surprises.

acme_ops: That would help. One more thing — we're seeing intermittent auth failures (401) during the spike window. Could that be related?

Lina (Platform Eng): If the gateway is overloaded it may drop requests before auth layer runs, producing 401-like responses if token validation cached results aren't available. Check your gateway logs for `auth error` vs `invalid token`. If you see `auth cache miss` spikes, raise auth cache TTL or prewarm caches.

acme_ops: We saw `authz: cache miss for key=acme-prod` around the same time. How to prewarm?

Maya (Support): Two options: 1) Prewarm by making lightweight authenticated heartbeat requests to warm caches, 2) Increase auth cache TTL in the gateway config (`auth_cache_ttl=60s`). We can propose a conservative TTL for you.

Raj (SRE): Repro steps we recommend for you to run and paste logs: 1) Run a 30s burst test (600 rps) with `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Request-ID: test-<n>"` and capture ingress/gateway logs. 2) Run `kubectl top pods` during test to watch CPU. 3) `kubectl exec` into ingress pod and `ss -s` to inspect socket states.

acme_ops: Example reproducer we used:
```
for i in {1..600}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: test-$i" https://api.acme.example/v1/generate &
done; wait
```

Lina (Platform Eng): After your tests, paste gateway debug logs (grep x-request-id). Also include `curl -I` to show response headers; we need `x-rate-limit-remaining`, `x-rate-limit-reset`, and `x-gateway-instance`.

Maya (Support): Action items:
- Support: create a temporary burst bump for API key and monitor (Raj)
- Customer: deploy client-side concurrency limits + retry with jitter (acme_ops)
- Customer: add nginx ingress annotations and kernel tweaks, run reproducer and paste logs (acme_ops)
- Platform Eng: propose a gateway config change for more permissive short bursts and TTL increase for auth cache (Lina)

acme_ops: Thanks — can you also confirm if any billing/quota implications for a temporary bump? We don't want surprise charges.

Maya (Support): Temporary bump will be noted on the account. It will increase allowed requests; actual billing is usage-based as usual. We'll set an auto-revert in 24h and alert you if spend exceeds a soft threshold.

Raj (SRE): I'll schedule the bump now. Expect a 10x burst window for next 1 hour. Please run your reproducer and paste logs.

ratebot: [automated] Burst policy change applied to key acme-prod by Raj at 2026-01-21T21:10:05Z — window=3600s, burst=450

acme_ops: Running the test again now. Will paste logs in ~10m. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): Closing loop once we have post-change logs. If 429s persist despite bump, we'll switch to per-route circuit breaker config and apply a short-lived queue on gateway to smooth spikes. :shipit:
